posts.title: Documentation in a Post-AI-Agent World
posts.description: The documentation for Docker Ansible has always had a fairly practical job: explain which image to pull, which tag to choose, what is inside it, and how to run it. As the project has accumulated Ansible Core versions, base operating systems, architectures and older tags, the README has become more than an introduction. It is an operational reference. posts.title: Improving home Wi-Fi: what the tests revealed
posts.description: I spent some time testing my home Wi-Fi properly this weekend, mainly because it felt “mostly fine” but not always great when the network was busy. The quick summary is: signal strength was never really the issue. In normal use, everything looked strong: Wi-Fi 6 on 5 GHz Signal around -40 dBm (excellent) Link rate up to 1200 Mbps Download around 450-460 Mbps Upload around 52-59 Mbps No packet loss
